title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. A 'disjoncteur' (E, |o|_E) is a set E with a symmetric 'disjointness' (orthogonality) relation |o|. It is extended to subsets: A |o| B means a |o| b for all a in A and b in B.

The operator supp°_E sends A ⊂ E to its 'support'. This is presumably the biorthogonal closure A^{oo}, where A^o = {y : y |o| A}. Σ_E is then the set of closed subsets ('supports'), a complete lattice with an orthocomplement-like involution A ↦ A^o.

The preceding page treated plain relations R ⊂ E×E'. There a correspondence α: E → P(E') extends to a Sup-preserving map ᾱ = α_*: P(E) → P(E'), and the transpose β satisfies ᾱ(A) ∩ A' = ∅ iff A ∩ β̄(A') = ∅.

This page generalises that to disjoncteurs. Take correspondences α: E → P(E') and β: E' → P(E), with additive extensions ᾱ and β̄. Prop. 3 states three equivalent conditions:
(i) for all x, x': x |o| β(x') ⟺ α(x) |o| x';
(ii) for all subsets A, A': A |o| β̄(A') ⟺ ᾱ(A) |o| A';
(iii) define α_*(𝔄) = supp°_{E'}(ᾱ(𝔄)) on Σ_E and β_* similarly. Then 𝔄 |o| β_*(𝔄') ⟺ α_*(𝔄) |o| 𝔄' on closed sets, together with the compatibilities α_*(supp° A) = supp°(ᾱ A) and β_*(supp° A') = supp°(β̄ A').
The margin gives the definition: α and β are then called 'transposed' to each other.

The Corollary (cut off at the page end) says these conditions depend only on the induced maps α_*, β_*: Σ_E ⇄ Σ_{E'}. In particular they are unchanged when α(x) is replaced by its support α'(x). The next page states that the transpose is unique up to support.

In modern terms this is the notion of adjoint (Galois-adjoint, 'dagger') morphisms between orthogonality spaces (orthosets), and of the induced adjointable maps between their complete ortholattices of closed subsets. It generalises the transpose of a relation and Galois connections / polarities. The purpose seems to be building a category of disjoncteurs with a transposition involution, in the 'Ateliers' notes of 1986.
errors: No real error. In (iii) it is ambiguous whether the compatibility relations α_*(supp A) = supp(ᾱA) are part of the condition or a consequence. In fact they follow from (i): x' |o| ᾱ(A) ⟺ β(x') |o| A ⟺ β(x') |o| A^{oo} ⟺ x' |o| ᾱ(A^{oo}), so ᾱ(A)^o = ᾱ(A^{oo})^o and the supports agree.
The proof of (iii) ⇒ (ii) is only announced on the next page; it is not done here.

ideas.what: Disjoncteur: a set with a symmetric disjointness relation, its closed subsets ('supports') Σ_E via biorthogonal closure
ideas.modern_name: orthogonality space / orthoset (Dacey), polarity closure system (Birkhoff)

ideas.what: Transposed correspondences α, β with x ⊥ β(x') ⟺ α(x) ⊥ x', and the induced adjoint maps α_*, β_* on closed sets
ideas.modern_name: adjoint maps between orthosets / adjointable (Foulis/Baer*-semigroup) maps of ortholattices / dagger structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Foulis (Baer *-semigroups, 1960s); Paseka–Vetterlein (categories of orthogonality spaces, ~2020s); Jacobs (dagger kernel categories, 2010); Heunen

ideas.what: Equivalence of pointwise, setwise and closure-level adjointness; independence from the choice of representative α vs. supp∘α
ideas.modern_name: adjunction descends to the lattice of closed sets
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore in quantum logic / Galois connection theory

missed.claim: In 1986 Grothendieck independently develops the theory of orthogonality spaces ('disjoncteurs') with adjoint ('transposed') morphisms. This is essentially the category of orthosets with adjointable maps, recently studied by Paseka–Vetterlein and Heunen in connection with dagger categories and Hilbert-space reconstruction. There is no record of Grothendieck working on quantum-logic-type structures.
missed.quote: Soient maintenant (E, |o|_E), (E', |o|_{E'}) deux disjoncteurs, et considérons deux correspondances α : E → P(E') ... on dit alors que α et β sont transposées l'une de l'autre
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a historically unknown independent approach to dagger/orthoset categories, a topic active today in categorical quantum foundations. The surrounding pages may contain further structural results, such as functoriality or a duality, worth comparing.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics on the page is elementary and known (adjoint maps of orthogonality spaces). However, Grothendieck developing 'disjoncteurs' with a transposition theory in 1986 is an unrecorded episode that connects to current orthoset/dagger-category research.
transcription_corrections: Lines 1-2 are hard to read. 'et l'on trouve la même interprétation pour la 2e moitié des α' is plausible; 'Bon' is likely a struck-out false start.

The margin likely reads 'Définition : on dit alors que α et β sont transposées l'une de l'autre' (written vertically on the left). The second vertical margin word may be 'demand(e)' rather than 'dans ce cas'.
'Cor.' is boxed and starts 'Ces conditions [ne dépendent que] des applications α_*, β_*'. The fragment 'en disjonction par des' is likely 'ne dépendent que des'.
In (iii) the struck-out text before Σ_E is probably 'P(E)'.
The final struck line is 'α'(x) = supp°_{E'} α(x)', consistent with the next page.
